# Percentage Composition in Chemistry

## Core Concept

Percentage composition tells you **what fraction (by mass) of each element is present in a compound**, expressed as a percentage.

---

## Formula

$$\% \text{ of an element} = \frac{\text{Total mass of that element in 1 mole of compound}}{\text{Molar mass of the compound}} \times 100$$

---

## Step-by-Step (Example: H₂O)

| Step | Action | Calculation |
|------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | Write the formula | H₂O |
| 2 | Find molar mass | (2 × 1) + 16 = **18 g/mol** |
| 3 | % of Hydrogen | (2 / 18) × 100 = **11.11%** |
| 4 | % of Oxygen | (16 / 18) × 100 = **88.89%** |
| 5 | Verify | 11.11 + 88.89 = **100%** ✓ |

---

## Key Points for MCQs

- The sum of all percentage compositions **always equals 100%**.
- It depends only on the **empirical formula**, not the sample size.
- It is used to determine the **empirical formula** from experimental data.
- Reverse problem: Given % composition → assume 100 g sample → convert to moles → find simplest whole-number ratio → empirical formula.

### Quick Reverse Example (Finding Empirical Formula)

> A compound is 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O.

| Element | Mass (assume 100 g) | Moles | Ratio (÷ smallest) |
|---------|---------------------|-------|--------------------|
| C | 40 | 40/12 = 3.33 | 1 |
| H | 6.7 | 6.7/1 = 6.7 | 2 |
| O | 53.3 | 53.3/16 = 3.33 | 1 |

→ Empirical formula = **CH₂O**

---
